findings.finding: Raw day-file wipe: every append_observation writes ONE new line to a fresh tmp file and then os.replace()s it over the whole daily .jsonl.gz, destroying all previously written rows of that day. Verified experimentally: 3 successful appends left exactly 1 row on disk. Plan §7 requires raw observations to be append-only. The live raw/ store is empty only because the WS is payload-silent under the ban; once streams flow, nearly every mark observation will be lost. The test suite never writes two distinct rows per day (test_raw_store_dedup_and_restart appends the same payload twice), so the defect passes. Remediate before G3 evidence is relied on.
findings.remediation_hint: Append to the existing day file (open day_path in gzip append, or read-modify-rewrite via tmp+fsync+rename), and add a multi-row-per-day regression test.

findings.finding: Half-open has no single-flight latch: at window expiry gate() records RECOVERING, re-arms state to RATE_LIMITED with the still-expired window, and returns None — so EVERY concurrent caller whose gate() lands between window expiry and the probe's observe_response() is also allowed through; the coalescer only merges identical canonical keys. Plan §5 'exactly ONE half-open probe ... everything else still suppressed' is not guaranteed under concurrency. Not triggered live (single probe caller in sidecar mode).
findings.remediation_hint: Add an explicit probe_in_flight flag set when the probe is released and cleared in observe_response/observe_success; suppress all other callers while set.

findings.finding: Re-open window ignores a fresh LONGER banned-until: live at 08:24:28Z the half-open probe's 418 body said 'banned until 10:18:44Z' (~114 min) but the re-open applied the doubling cap and set allowed_retry_at = 08:39:28Z, scheduling repeated half-open probes INSIDE the venue's stated ban window (≈1 probe/15 min until ~10:18Z). The letter of §5's doubling cap is implemented, but the interaction contradicts §5 longer-wins and the §15 hard stop 'no Binance retry inside an active Retry-After window'. Bounded (single counted probe per 15 min), but the window law should floor with the fresh banned-until expiry.
findings.remediation_hint: On re-open, allowed_retry_at = max(opened_at + min(doubled_window, 15min), fresh Retry-After/banned-until expiry).

findings.finding: Datum truth-labeling gaps: (a) provenance is hardcoded 'ws_event' and source is the WS channel even when the last value came from the REST freshness probe (apply_rest_mark), so REST-sourced payloads are mislabeled — plan §4 requires the payload to stay labeled with its REST source and §6 requires response_sha256 provenance for REST-sourced data; (b) surface_state derives only from the WS breaker, so the REST surface's RATE_LIMITED never forces the datum status — verified live: BTCUSDT reads status STALE / surface_state HEALTHY while /v1/status.rest_breaker = RATE_LIMITED; the cause of staleness is invisible in the datum contract §6 says must force RATE_LIMITED.
findings.remediation_hint: Track the value's source on SymbolDatum (ws_event vs rest endpoint + response_sha256) and propagate REST RATE_LIMITED into surface_state/status when the WS is simultaneously silent.

findings.finding: Plan-mandated durable events are missing from the append-only EventLog: 'non_retryable_status' (§5/FND-2 remediation promise) exists only as an exception kind + in-memory breaker record; 'eviction_refetch' (§7) exists only as an in-memory counter, and eviction logging writes 'cache_evicted_bytes' instead; 'slow_consumer' (§8) exists only as in-memory dropped_reason — and the dropped consumer is removed from the fanout map WITHOUT its websocket being closed, so the client silently stops receiving. Breaker history itself is memory-only (lost on restart), so §5 'error history append-only, never truncated by restart' is only partially durable.
findings.remediation_hint: Append these event kinds to EventLog; close the slow consumer's websocket on drop; persist breaker transitions (or reconstruct from EventLog) across restart.

findings.finding: 5xx bounded-retry budget exceeds the frozen law: plan §5(c) says 5xx without Retry-After gets bounded retry ≤2, but the implementation shares ONE transport budget of 4 retries across all retryable causes (timeouts, network errors, 5xx), so a pure 5xx sequence is retried 4 times before TransportExhausted. Each retry is min-gap paced and 3 consecutive 5xx do raise DEGRADED, but the per-call bound deviates from the plan.
findings.remediation_hint: Add a dedicated 5xx-retry counter capped at 2 within _fetch_upstream, separate from the transport-timeout budget.

findings.finding: §12 frozen test-list gaps and two weak tests: MISSING — WS reconnect test (grep: no reconnect test anywhere), one-upstream-connection test (≤190 symbols ⇒ exactly 1 WS connection), bounded network-timeout test, and a 5xx bounded-retry behavior test (only classification-level). WEAK — test_ws_freshness_probe_only_when_degraded contains a no-op stub ('await ... if False else None', line 327) and never exercises the actual probe-loop degraded gating; test_cache_eviction_budget asserts the tautology 'removed > 0 or cache.evictions >= 0'. The canary abort-wait computation max(RA, banned-until, 120s) is also not unit-tested (validated only by live leg A evidence).
findings.remediation_hint: Add the four missing §12 tests; replace the stub with a real ws_freshness_probe_loop iteration; make the eviction test assert evictions >= 1 with a shrunk cap.

findings.finding: WS breaker telemetry dead path: note_ws_state is never called (grep-verified), so ws_breaker stays HEALTHY while the stream is down; gap_scan_loop assigns ws_breaker.state = 'GAP_DETECTED' directly, bypassing _record, so that transition is absent from breaker history. surface_state() patches payloads but /v1/status.ws_breaker can mislead.
findings.remediation_hint: Call note_ws_state on stream connect/disconnect and route the gap transition through _record.

findings.finding: Completeness truth nits: the gap list is silently truncated to 50 entries with no truncation flag (complete:false still truthful), and funding windows report complete=True with no cadence check (documented judgment call in code; plan freezes no funding grid). No interpolation occurs anywhere — gaps are listed, never filled.
findings.remediation_hint: Add gaps_truncated flag; consider marking funding completeness null/unknown instead of true.

findings.finding: API/lifecycle drift: /v1/bars|basis|funding take startMs/endMs and ignore the §6-documented start&end[&limit] params (shape drift, harmless); graceful shutdown does not flush consumer queues within 5 s — shutdown_flush only persists seq and the ws sender tasks die with runner.cleanup, so buffered events (≤2000/consumer) are lost on shutdown (consumers must replay on reconnect).
findings.remediation_hint: Accept start/end aliases and a limit param; drain consumer queues up to 5 s before closing in shutdown().

findings.finding: Two defense-in-depth gaps: EventLog rotation deletes the previous .1 sidecar (history bounded at ~2×40MB — 'never truncated by restart' holds literally, but old incidents are eventually discarded); GatewayConfig.load accepts any bind value from a config file and run_service performs no loopback validation — the default is 127.0.0.1 and no non-loopback config exists (lsof verified loopback-only), but the §3 'no 0.0.0.0/LAN' hard boundary is operator-trust, not code-enforced.
findings.remediation_hint: Keep 3 rotation generations; hard-assert bind in ('127.0.0.1','localhost') in run_service.

findings.finding: Unknown worker heartbeat (None) maps to worker LIVE / badge not-OFFLINE — fail-open labeling for the OFFLINE badge ('heartbeat dead'). Consumed only after post-GO cutover step 1; pure function is tested for the explicit states but None-heartbeat optimism is untested.
findings.remediation_hint: Treat heartbeat age None as OFFLINE (or UNKNOWN) rather than LIVE.

summary: Round-2 implementation audit of LIVE-DATA-GATEWAY-V1 at cb8bdf18c9dc0693d976b28d65b31410809b968d (branch orca/live-data-gateway-v1-integration). Verdict: AUTHORIZED_WITH_FINDINGS — 0 CRITICAL / 1 HIGH / 6 MEDIUM / 6 LOW. The sidecar implementation is live and behaving truthfully under the active shared-IP ban: loopback-only bind verified via lsof; exactly ONE upstream REST call ever issued (418 -> 800s banned-until window), all subsequent probes suppressed and counted; a single half-open probe fired at window expiry and the window doubled into the 15-min cap; all symbols honestly STALE with canonical_current false; 404 for unsubscribed; existing workers (pids 15315/65461) alive with updating heartbeats and a byte-clean SHV1 worktree; no order/broker/credential surface; canary code carries the frozen §9.2 thresholds verbatim and its direct leg demonstrably stopped issuing after the 418 abort. The HIGH finding (FND-1) is an experimentally-confirmed raw-store defect: each observation replaces the daily .jsonl.gz, so the §7 append-only raw store silently loses all but the last row per day — currently masked because the WS is payload-silent; it must be fixed (with a regression test) before G3 evidence relies on raw-store completeness; the canary verdict path (research/control/.../canary/) is unaffected. MEDIUMs: half-open multi-probe concurrency hole, banned-until-vs-15-min-cap re-probe scheduling observed live, REST-provenance mislabeling + RATE_LIMITED not propagated into datums, missing durable events (non_retryable_status/eviction_refetch/slow_consumer) + slow-consumer ws never closed, 5xx retry budget 4 vs frozen ≤2, and §12 test-list gaps (WS reconnect, one-upstream-connection, bounded timeout, 5xx behavior) plus one stub and one tautology test. Measured tests: 64 passed / 0 failed (g1_evidence.json says 63 at the earlier commit — FND-8, refresh it). Canary/G3 adjudication is explicitly WAITING: leg A has accumulated only minutes of rows so far, leg B has not yet produced leg_b_history.jsonl (first attempt crashed against the pre-fix gateway; driver retries every 30 min); the ≥24 h dual-run verdict is NOT_RUN/WAITING and is not audited here.
